reviewer: Claude (independent read-only review; did not author the supervisor)
verdict: APPROVED FOR ITS STATED ROLE, WITH NOTES. The enum command, its return-code mapping, the endpoint wait loop and the strict registry gate call are identical to the reviewed passive-child c361a868 and two-window 0ffade27 supervisors (only marker names differ). The fixed parent /usr/bin/darwin-spawn-whitelist-parent's actual return code is retained. The closed exporter runs whether or not the parent failed. STATUS prints both return codes. The RETURN/uname/END footer appears only when both are 0. There is no compositor, Wayland, human prompt or input. The parent fixture is still moving and was not reviewed, so no spawn or descriptor result follows.

binding.script: sha256 recomputed as b8a667c2 = source-validation script_sha256. revisions/001 recomputes as a4205ea4.
binding.rev001_to_rev002_diff: Only lines 25-28 changed: the records_rc capture with a fixed exporter call, STATUS gaining records=, and the footer gate requiring both values to be 0.
binding.exporter_reference: closed_exporter_source_set 37d3d535 equals the frozen records manifest (reviewed separately in managed-spawn-records-source-review.json). The exporter path /usr/bin/darwin-spawn-records matches the build.nix output name.

checks.nonce: Empty input, a non-[0-9a-f] character, uppercase or a wrong length exits 2 before any output (lines 4-6). Rechecked on scratch under bash --posix: 7 malformed forms gave rc 2 with 0 bytes of output.
checks.prefix_equivalence: The enum, wait and gate command lines extracted from c361a868 and 0ffade27 are identical apart from marker prefixes. The new script stops after the gate (no runtime directory, Wayland wait or clients).
checks.control_flow_stubs_scratch: A scratch copy had only paths substituted: /usr/bin to stub binaries, and the HID nodes to existing character devices. Results: all 0 gives STATUS probe=0 records=0, the footer, rc 0. probe=3 means the exporter still runs, STATUS probe=3 records=0, no footer, rc 1. records=1 gives rc 1 with no footer. probe=77 with records=1 gives STATUS probe=77 records=1 and rc 1. enum=77 exits 77 after the ENUM line, before the gate. gate=5 exits 1 after the IDENTITY line, before the parent. Under set -e, return codes are captured with 'if cmd; then :; else rc=$?; fi', which is POSIX-correct.
checks.no_ui: The script starts no compositor or client, sets no Wayland environment, prompts for nothing and injects no input. Its physical_input_proven=false labels are on BEGIN, STATUS and END.

notes.S1_no_local_timeouts: The parent and exporter calls have no timeout in the script. Bounds come from the unreviewed parent and the host's 180 s limit; a hang must be preserved as a host-timeout failure.
notes.S2_closed_depends_on_parent: 'closed' assumes the parent has exited and reaped every writer of /private/tmp/chonk-spawn-whitelist-<nonce>. The exporter detects growth only during its own read. This is a parent-fixture contract item for its own review.
notes.S3_shared_console: Parent output shares the capture. Any DL19_RECORD_ line from the parent makes the decode fail closed; it cannot spoof a record, because the real lines then repeat. The parent should not use that prefix.
notes.S4_probe_77: A parent rc of 77 becomes script exit 1, whereas enum and gate 77 map to exit 77. The raw parent rc is kept in STATUS, so classification must read STATUS rather than the script's exit code.
notes.S5_extra_arguments: Arguments after a valid nonce are ignored: '<nonce> extra' ran to rc 0 on scratch. The fixed launcher passes exactly one.
notes.S6_failure_markers: Enum and gate failures print only their rc line before exiting, without c361a868's explicit NOT_READY/FAILED lines. The cause is still recorded because the rc line comes first. ENUM, WAIT and IDENTITY lines drop the physical_input_proven=false label.
notes.S7_directory: The script neither creates nor checks the records directory. If it is absent or unsafe, the exporter returns 1 and the decode is incomplete.

not_claimed: Darwin FD whitelist or spawn evidence
